exclude_why.cicada/cics/cell.py: The one mutable slot CicsRegion keeps its position in. A pseudo-conversational region is a cursor over (transid, program, commarea) that advances each turn; the position itself is a frozen value replaced wholesale here, so the rest of dispatcher.py stays gated. exclude_why.tests/: The rules target production style, while fixtures legitimately mutate -- `region[0:8] = data` on a bytearray reads better than any concatenation satisfying no-subscript-mutation. The suites also predate this gate, so touching one file for an unrelated reason surfaces its whole backlog and blocks the commit.
exclude_why.cobble/cobble/asg_walk.py: The corpus's one ASG descent. It walks a document whose nesting outruns CPython's recursion limit, so the stack must be explicit -- no-list-append/no-list-pop/no-loop-mutation cannot all be met. Constraint comes from the ASG, not from style.
exclude_why.cobble/cobble/dataflow/srccfg/worklist.p: The reaching-definitions worklist. It updates one node's out mask and the pending set in place as the fixpoint converges; an immutable rebuild per step or full sweeps is the path it replaced (837s against under a second on the largest member measured, 9f3aad14), so no-subscript-mutation/no-loop-mutation/no-set-add cannot be met without that cost. Only the loop lives here, so the rest of dataflow.py stays gated.
exclude_why.cobble/cobble/dataflow/fixpoint/rows.py: The JSONL boundary, and it exists so that `object` appears in one place instead of across the query surface. json.loads returns whatever the file held; a recursive `str | int | Sequence[Json] | ...` alias renames that ignorance without adding a check, satisfying no-object-type in word and not in spirit. Everything above the boundary works in str/int/tuple[str, ...].
exclude_why.cobble/cobble/dataflow/fixpoint/fixpoint: A deferred backlog, not a design constraint: the sweep in `_propagated` and the loop in `_swept` carry all nine, and `_eta`/`_propagated` trip C901 at 4 > 3. Pinning python-fp-lint to a concrete rev turned the previously inert ruleset on, so the file began failing without being touched and blocked a rename that changed one import line in it. Whether a worklist fixpoint earns the mutation the way asg_walk.py's explicit stack does is the open question. See forge-uar.
exclude_why.cobble/cobble/dataflow/depgraph/: A deferred backlog, not a design constraint: the five files carry 145 of that package's 167 violations, all accumulator loops and nesting depth. `rev: main` in .pre-commit-config.yaml tracks a mutable ruleset, so they began failing without being touched, and pre-existing violations in a file blocked commits to it for unrelated reasons. See red-dragon-forge-bgk.
exclude_why.cobble/cobble/viz/render_cmd.py: HTML string assembly. The renderer builds Mermaid and vis.js payloads by accumulating lines and node/edge dicts; every alternative (nested list comprehensions over a recursive step tree, reduce over a mutable JS template) is less readable and no more correct. The rendering logic carries no domain logic and no state that outlives a single render call.
exclude_why.cicada/cics/tn3270/wire.py: The telnet byte stream. A socket delivers unframed bytes; turning them into telnet events and EOR-delimited records needs read buffers filled in place, and the accept loop runs until the process stops. Negotiation and session logic over these events stay gated.
exclude_why.squall/squall/exec_sql_scan.py: The EXEC SQL / END-EXEC cursor-advancing scan, now matched over parsed FixedLine code areas (squall.fixed_format) rather than raw source text -- the sequence-number handling this used to carry (a `(?:\d{6})?` regex prefix, and a second regex stripping leading digits from every parse_text line) is gone entirely, since a code area cannot contain sequence digits by construction. A functional recursive-unfold rewrite (in place of the accumulate-and-append while loop) passed every unit test but raised RecursionError at roughly 1000 EXEC SQL statements in one source file (verified: 900 passes, 1200 crashes) -- a real regression on a shared package, since the original loop had no such bound. This is a lexer over a cursor position by nature; the iterative loop here has no depth ceiling. Only the scan (Span, the span-finding loop, its match-to-span/line-offset helpers) lives here; classification and rewriting stay gated in preprocess.py.
exclude_why.squall/squall/strategy_stores.py: The SQL lowering strategy's writes into state it does not own, each read back by its owner as the same object: builtin registration into the VM's process-global Builtins.TABLE, the __exec_sql builtin's closed-over plan-pool list, and the field_meta store the same builtin's MappingProxyType view already wraps (forge-yuo). Mirrors cicada/cics/strategy_stores.py's justification exactly -- a rebuilt copy of any of the three would go unseen by its reader. Only those stores live here; every lowering decision stays gated in strategy.py.
exclude_why.squall/squall/strategy.py: Four violations, all structurally forced, not deferred debt: (1) no-subscript-mutation on self._whenever[...] = ... (line 241) -- state the strategy owns for its own lifetime (condition -> action), unlike the three stores extracted to strategy_stores.py; a rebuild-and-reassign here has no external reader to orphan, but the rule can't tell owned state from shared state. (2) no-list-dict-param-annotation on preprocess_program_dict's `data: dict` (line 183) -- RedDragonExtensionLoweringStrategy (vendor/red-dragon/interpreter/frontend_extension_lowering.py) declares that exact signature; squall does not own the Protocol. (3)+(4) no-object-type on handles()'s (line 178) and lower()'s (line 212) `stmt: object` -- the Protocol declares `stmt: Any`; ANN401 (a blocking Ruff check) forbids Any in squall's own signatures, and object is the only type both narrower than Any and inline with the Protocol's own contravariance. python-fp-lint has no rule that is satisfied by both no-object-type and ANN401 simultaneously for an Any-typed Protocol parameter. The constructor's `stores: SharedSqlStores | None = None` + `if stores is None` this branch briefly added (and the two `.update()` calls that duplicated `absorb_field_meta`) are gone, not re-justified: `stores` now defaults to `strategy_stores.ABSENT` (a dedicated sentinel type, not `None`) and the field_meta/sidecar-names merge now calls `absorb_field_meta` directly -- zero net new violations, and the constructor's own duplication of coprocessor.py's precedence logic is gone too.
exclude_why.squall/squall/builtins/exec_sql.py: Seven violations (was four; three added this branch for open_cursors, enumerated below rather than re-blessed as a round number): the connection state a real CICS-attached Db2 session can genuinely be in before any EXEC SQL CONNECT runs is disconnected, and None is DbConnector.connect()'s own return type for 'no such backend' (squall.connector, a protocol this file does not own) -- every no-is-none, no-list-dict-param-annotation and C901/PLR0915/B008 violation this file used to carry (task-6 brief) was fixed directly (match/case on the connection, Sequence/Mapping annotations, extracted helpers, a module-level NullDbConnector() singleton). (1)+(2) no-optional-none on _ConnState.current (line 103) and _current()'s return type (line 129) -- both are exactly that Optional<SqlBackend> from the connector protocol, threaded through rather than re-wrapped in a private sentinel that would just mean the same 'no backend' one term over. (3) no-unfrozen-dataclass on _ConnState (line 98) -- the one per-run mutable cell every EXEC SQL CONNECT/SET CONNECTION/DISCONNECT statement reassigns in place, mirroring cicada/cics/cell.py's Cell for the identical reason (a rebuild has no external reader to update). (4) no-subscript-mutation on ctx.cursors[name] = parsed in _h_declare_cursor (line 211) -- the per-run cursor registry every later OPEN/FETCH/CLOSE reads back by name; a rebuilt copy would go unseen by them, the same justification as strategy_stores.py's stores. (5) no-set-add on ctx.open_cursors.add(name) in _open_declared_cursor (line 230), (6) no-set-discard on ctx.open_cursors.discard(name) in _h_close (line 281), (7) no-dict-clear on ctx.open_cursors.clear() in _close_all_cursors (line 315) -- open_cursors is the same shape of per-run shared mutable state as ctx.cursors above (see _Ctx's own docstring on what it answers): OPEN/FETCH/CLOSE/task-end all read the SAME set object back, so a rebuilt copy would go unseen by them too. What is NOT here any more: make_exec_sql_builtin's `cursors: dict[...] | None = None` and its `cursors is not None` check, this branch's fifth addition -- eliminated, not documented, by giving `cursors` the same `strategy_stores.ABSENT` sentinel default `stores` uses in strategy.py, so the default is a fresh private dict without an admission-of-None pair.
exclude_why.squall/squall/backends/_stores.py: One violation, structurally forced: no-subscript-mutation on cursors[name] = value in set_cursor. SqliteBackend/Db2Backend each own one _cursors dict for their instance's lifetime; a later fetch/close call reads it back by name, so a rebuilt copy would go unseen -- the same shape strategy_stores.py exists for. It is a separate module, not a reuse of strategy_stores.py, because strategy_stores.py imports squall.parser.sql_model and .importlinter's parser-backends-independence contract forbids squall.backends from importing anything under squall.parser, even transitively (task-7 brief, forge-qhi).
exclude_why.squall/squall/binding_stores.py: Two violations, both structurally forced: no-subscript-mutation applying (offset, bytes) writes into the WS region bytearray in apply_writes (every SQLCODE/SQLERRM/host-var write squall.binding makes), and no-list-insert prepending red-dragon's vendor checkout to sys.path in bootstrap_vendor_path (the one process-global mutation binding.py needs at import time). Extracted out of squall.binding (task-8 review round 1: binding.py itself carries no fp.json entry and is fully linted) so that module's own code stays pure -- it computes writes/paths, this leaf module is the one place that applies them, the same shape strategy_stores.py and backends/_stores.py exist for.
